title: Dishmachine lease + chemical subscription route for independent foodservice (Auto-Chlor model)
product_service: Low-temp chemical-sanitizing dishmachines and bar glasswashers placed on lease (or customer-owned machines brought onto program), bundled with metered detergent/sanitizer/rinse-aid, scheduled preventive maintenance roughly every 4 weeks, and 24/7 emergency repair.
target_customer: Owner/GM of independent restaurants, bars, daycare centers, churches, small senior-living and school kitchens (1-3 machines each) in Chicagoland.
purchase_motivation: Health-code sanitizing requirement; a broken dishmachine stops service; avoids $5-15k machine capex [E]; one vendor for machine, chemicals and repair.
spending_evidence: Warewashing products were ~13% of Ecolab's $16.1B 2025 consolidated sales (~$2B) [A, WS13-S005]; Auto-Chlor claims 140 branches and >100,000 customers [D, WS13-S006] on a lease + 28-day route-service model [D, WS13-S007].
representative_operators: Ecolab - Global Institutional & Specialty segment $5.96B sales, 22.8% operating margin in 2025 (incumbent economics) [A, WS13-S005]
Auto-Chlor System - ~140 branches, >100k customers, leased machines + chemicals + route service (company claim) [D, WS13-S006]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly bundled fee per account (machine + chemicals + service) or chemical-volume pricing with free dispensing equipment; parts/repairs billed for customer-owned machines.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING verified price; analyst estimate $150-$450 per account per month [E].
direct_costs: Chemicals (distributor-supplied or toll-blended private label), machine depreciation (est. $3-8k per door-type low-temp machine [E]), route technician labor, parts, van.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $90-$220/month per account after chemicals, parts and route labor at ~40-60 accounts per technician [E].
working_capital_note: Machine capex precedes 24-36 months of fee recovery; chemical inventory; restaurant net-15/30 receivables; closures strand placed machines.
sales_cycle: 2-8 weeks; owner-level decision, often triggered by a machine failure or poor service from current vendor.
acquisition_channels: door-to-door to independent restaurants and bars
referrals from restaurant equipment repair techs and used-equipment dealers
customer_accessibility: Buyers are numerous and identifiable from public license data; owner-operators are busy and many are under Ecolab/Auto-Chlor/distributor programs; switching is easiest at a service failure.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: dishmachines available via manufacturer dealers and used market; EPA-registered sanitizers via chemical distributors or toll blenders (private label requires registration work) [E].
competitive_intensity: high - Ecolab, Auto-Chlor, broadline-distributor chemical programs, local chemical dealers.
entry_strategy: Owner-run local responsiveness (same-day service), month-to-month terms, transparent pricing for small independents that national players under-serve; bundle glasswashers for bars.
licenses: No specific Illinois license for dishmachine service identified [E]; sanitizers must be EPA/FIFRA-registered products used per label; new plumbing/electrical hookups may need licensed trades in Chicago [E, unverified]; general liability insurance.
regulatory_barriers: Antimicrobial pesticide labeling/repackaging rules if private-labeling sanitizer; hazmat handling of corrosive concentrates.
operational_risks: Technician hiring; 24/7 emergency coverage; chemical spills/burns; machine reliability.
financial_risks: Restaurant failure rate strands capital; price competition from bundled distributor programs.
geographic_constraints: Route density business; start in one dense suburb cluster or Chicago neighborhood.
founder_expertise: Dishmachine mechanics, sanitation chemistry, food-code requirements, field sales.
staffing: Founder sells and services first ~40 accounts; first technician at ~50-70 accounts; office/dispatch at ~150.
automation_potential: Route optimization, digital service logs for health inspections, dispenser telemetry where available, prospect lists from license data, quoting/billing; hands-on service stays human.
delegation_potential: Good: route technician and sales roles are standard; Auto-Chlor's branch network shows replicable branch model.
scalability: Branch-by-branch replication across Midwest metros; recurring revenue base compounds.
expansion: On-premise laundry chemicals for hotels/nursing homes, housekeeping chemicals, glasswashers, ice-machine subscriptions (WS13-002), beer-line cleaning (WS13-010).
roic_note: ~$40-80k capital (van, tools, first 30-60 placed machines) for $60-250k operating profit implies ~100-300% if account retention holds [E].
critical_assumptions: Independent operators will switch from incumbents for service/price
Private or distributor chemical supply at margins near 40%+
unanswered_questions: Actual monthly pricing charged by Auto-Chlor/Ecolab to small accounts
Used/new low-temp machine cost and service life
Whether Illinois requires any registration for sanitizer distribution
failure_modes: Over-investing in machines placed at failing restaurants
Competing only on price against Ecolab bundles
score_rationale: Resilience 7: sanitation is code-required and chemicals are consumed weekly. Scale 7: a private incumbent runs ~140 branches on the template. Access/entry 5: entrenched national players; wedge is local service. FCF 5: plausible $100-150k by yr 3-5 with 2-3 techs.
preliminary_verdict: advance - recurring consumable route with proven private-company template; validate small-account pricing and chemical supply.

title: Commercial ice-machine subscription (ice-as-a-service) for restaurants, bars, healthcare and hotels
subindustry: Ice machine leasing with included cleaning/repair
product_service: Commercial ice machines (undercounter, modular head+bin, dispensers) placed for a monthly fee that includes installation, sanitizing/descaling 2-4x per year, repairs, replacement and backup ice.
target_customer: Owners/facility managers at restaurants, bars, c-stores, clinics, dental/surgery centers, hotels, senior living, gyms.
purchase_motivation: Ice machines are dirty and failure-prone; health-inspection findings (mold/slime); avoid $3-10k capex [E]; predictable opex.
spending_evidence: Easy Ice publishes subscription prices from $170/mo (undercounter) to $460/mo (large modular) [B, WS13-S008] and has rolled up regional ice-subscription operators across 47 states [D, WS13-S009].
representative_operators: Easy Ice - national ice-machine subscription roll-up, 47 states (company claim) [D, WS13-S009]
Local refrigeration contractors offering lease programs [E]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly subscription per machine (36-60-month typical term assumed [E]); add-on cleaning-only contracts for customer-owned machines.
typical_transaction_value: $170-$460 per machine per month at incumbent list price [B, WS13-S008]; new-entrant realized price likely 10-25% lower [E].
direct_costs: Machine depreciation (purchase price MISSING; est. $3-8k installed [E]), filters, sanitizer/descaler, technician time, refrigeration parts, warranty claims.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $90-$220/machine/month after depreciation and service at list-like pricing [E].
working_capital_note: Each placement requires $3-8k up front recovered over ~2-3 years [E]; equipment financing likely needed for growth; monthly billing in advance possible.
sales_cycle: 1-6 weeks; triggered by machine failure, health citation or new opening.
acquisition_channels: restaurant equipment dealers and repair techs
customer_accessibility: High-urgency moments (failure) create inbound demand; many buyers; national incumbent markets heavily online.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: major ice-machine brands sell through dealers/distributors; dealer agreements may restrict rental programs [E].
competitive_intensity: moderate - Easy Ice nationally, refrigeration contractors locally; many buyers still purchase outright.
entry_strategy: Bundle with dish/chemical route (WS13-001) - same customer, same visit cadence; faster local repair than national subscription firm.
licenses: EPA Section 608 technician certification for refrigerant work (exam-based, federal) [E]; possibly Chicago refrigeration/plumbing licensing for water hookups [E, unverified].
regulatory_barriers: Refrigerant transition rules (AIM Act) affect equipment choice [E].
operational_risks: Repair skill depth; parts lead times; backup-ice logistics in summer peaks.
financial_risks: Capital per account; early cancellations; residual value of used machines.
geographic_constraints: Route density; one metro at a time.
founder_expertise: Commercial refrigeration repair, water treatment basics, equipment finance.
automation_potential: Scheduling, inventory of machine fleet, IoT monitoring on newer machines, billing.
delegation_potential: Technician roles standard but refrigeration techs are scarce and well paid.
scalability: Capital-bound; scale funded by equipment financing and retained earnings.
expansion: Water filtration, beverage equipment, dishmachines, walk-in cooler maintenance.
roic_note: Asset-heavy per account: ~30-60% annual return on machine capital at list-like pricing [E].
critical_assumptions: Machine cost and life allow ~2-3 year payback
Customers accept 3-5 year subscriptions from a new local firm
unanswered_questions: Wholesale machine costs and dealer restrictions
Typical service hours per machine per year
score_rationale: Pricing is published (B) and a roll-up exists, showing durable cash; but capital per account and refrigeration-tech scarcity cap ROIC and delegation.
preliminary_verdict: advance - pair with WS13-001 as a foodservice equipment-as-a-service route; validate machine costs and contract terms.

title: Point-of-use (bottleless) water cooler and filtered dispenser rental to workplaces
product_service: Plumbed-in filtered hot/cold water dispensers and bottle fillers rented monthly with filter changes and sanitizing; optional ice/water combo units.
target_customer: Office managers/plant managers at warehouses, factories, clinics, schools, gyms, auto dealers (25-500 occupants).
purchase_motivation: Cheaper and less hassle than 5-gallon jug delivery; sustainability; employee amenity.
spending_evidence: Culligan Quench models bottleless at ~$62-$118/month for 25-100 daily users vs $253-$691 for jug delivery; installation from $199 [C, WS13-S010]; Cintas reports workplace water services inside its $1.39B First Aid & Safety segment [A, WS13-S003].
representative_operators: Culligan Quench - national POU provider [C, WS13-S010]
Cintas - workplace water within First Aid & Safety segment [A, WS13-S003]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly rental per unit ($40-$120 [E]) + installation fee.
typical_transaction_value: ~$60-$120/month per unit at incumbent modeled cost [C, WS13-S010].
direct_costs: Dispenser capex (est. $500-1,500 [E]), filters, sanitizing visits, install parts.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $35-$80/unit/month after filter and visit costs [E].
working_capital_note: Unit capex recovered in ~12-24 months [E]; monthly billing.
customer_accessibility: Many buyers; low ticket means sales cost matters; post-2020 office occupancy lower.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: POU units and filters available from manufacturers/distributors [E].
competitive_intensity: high - Culligan, Primo/ReadyRefresh, Cintas, local dealers.
entry_strategy: Industrial/warehouse segment where national players bundle less; bundle with first-aid route (WS13-004).
licenses: Plumbing connection may require licensed plumber in some municipalities [E, unverified].
financial_risks: Low ticket; churn when offices move.
founder_expertise: Basic plumbing, water treatment, B2B selling.
automation_potential: Filter-change scheduling, billing, prospecting.
scalability: Moderate; low ticket limits profit per route.
expansion: Coffee service, ice machines, micro-markets, first aid.
roic_note: High per-unit ROIC (~50-100%/yr on unit capex) but small absolute profits [E].
critical_assumptions: Industrial accounts accept rental from a small local firm
failure_modes: Low ticket cannot support sales cost
score_rationale: Good unit economics and delegation, but crowded with national bundlers and small tickets cap FCF.
preliminary_verdict: hold - better as an add-on SKU on a first-aid/hygiene route than a standalone business.

title: Independent first-aid cabinet restocking & safety-supply van route (with AED/eyewash compliance)
product_service: Monthly/bi-monthly van visits to restock wall-mounted first-aid cabinets, plus sale of PPE, eyewash stations, burn kits, AED pads/batteries tracking, and basic safety signage; compliance log provided to the site.
target_customer: Plant managers, safety coordinators, office managers at factories, warehouses, contractors, auto shops, restaurants (10-500 employees).
purchase_motivation: Workplace first-aid availability is an OSHA expectation (29 CFR 1910.151, text not retrieved this session) [E]; avoids self-managed stock-outs; insurer/auditor checks.
spending_evidence: Cintas First Aid & Safety Services revenue $1,391.9M in FY2026 (+14.3%), gross margin 57.7%, operating margin 25.4% [A, WS13-S003] - incumbent economics.
representative_operators: Cintas First Aid & Safety - $1.39B segment revenue, 25.4% operating margin (incumbent) [A, WS13-S003]
Local/regional independent first-aid van distributors [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-item replenishment billing at each visit + optional cabinet service fee; product sales margin.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING verified; analyst estimate $40-$150 per site per month [E].
direct_costs: Product COGS from medical/safety wholesalers, van and fuel, route driver-sales rep pay.
contribution_profit_note: Est. $20-$80 per site per month after COGS and route time; ~250-400 sites per route rep [E].
working_capital_note: Van inventory ~$5-10k; net-30 B2B receivables; low capex per account (cabinet often sold or loaned).
acquisition_channels: displacing Cintas accounts after uniform/mat price increases
referrals from safety consultants and insurance loss-control reps
customer_accessibility: Very identifiable buyers; low switching cost; incumbents bundle with uniforms which can create dissatisfaction during consolidation (Cintas-UniFirst merger agreement) [A, WS13-S004].
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: first-aid and PPE wholesalers sell to independent distributors; private-label kits available [E].
competitive_intensity: high - Cintas plus regional distributors; but service quality varies.
entry_strategy: Fixed-price transparency, no auto-renew contracts, faster visits; target accounts dissatisfied with bundled national contracts.
licenses: No license for non-prescription first-aid supplies identified [E]; avoid Rx/OTC drug repackaging; AED sales may involve medical-device distribution rules [E].
operational_risks: Route-rep turnover; inventory shrink; expired product.
geographic_constraints: Route density in industrial corridors (Chicago suburbs suit).
founder_expertise: Safety product knowledge, OSHA basics, route sales.
staffing: Founder runs first route; hire route sales reps at ~250 accounts each.
automation_potential: Visit scheduling, usage analytics per site, automated invoices and compliance logs, prospect lists from business registries.
delegation_potential: High - route sales rep is an established job category.
scalability: Multi-route, multi-metro; adjacent SKUs raise ticket.
expansion: Eyewash/AED programs, PPE vending, workplace water (WS13-003), restroom hygiene (WS13-005), CPR/first-aid training (WS09).
roic_note: Low capital (<$25k) against $50-200k profit implies very high ROIC once routes are dense [E].
critical_assumptions: Independents can achieve ~40%+ gross margin without scale buying
failure_modes: Sub-scale routes with too much drive time
score_rationale: ROIC 8: inventory-light route with A-level incumbent margins (57.7% GM). Access 6: buyers easy to find, switching cheap. Entry 5: wedge is service; easily copied.
preliminary_verdict: advance - low-capital consumable route with A-level incumbent profitability evidence; core of a multi-SKU workplace route.

title: Restroom hygiene service route (sanitary disposal units, air care, soap/sanitizer dispensers)
product_service: Placement and periodic exchange/servicing of sanitary napkin disposal units, metered air fresheners, urinal screens, toilet-seat sanitizers, soap/sanitizer dispensers with refills.
target_customer: Facility/office managers at offices, schools, restaurants, gyms, medical offices, retail, churches.
purchase_motivation: Hygiene expectations and complaints; outsourcing a messy task; consistent consumable supply.
spending_evidence: Cintas sells restroom cleaning services and supplies within its $8.6B Uniform Rental & Facility Services segment [A, WS13-S003]; specific spend per site MISSING.
representative_operators: Cintas - restroom services within facility services [A, WS13-S003]
Rentokil Initial (Initial Hygiene) [E, not verified this session]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly or per-service fee per unit placed, plus consumables.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING; analyst estimate $5-$20 per unit per month, 5-20 units per site [E].
direct_costs: Disposal liners/bags, refills, units (low cost), route labor, sanitary-waste disposal.
working_capital_note: Low unit capex; consumables inventory; net-30.
customer_accessibility: Good; janitorial contractors are a channel; many small sites.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: unit and refill manufacturers sell to independent distributors [E].
competitive_intensity: moderate - Cintas, hygiene specialists, janitorial companies.
entry_strategy: Sell through janitorial contractors as white-label hygiene subcontractor; bundle on same van as first aid.
licenses: Sanitary hygiene waste handling: whether Illinois treats it as regulated medical waste is MISSING [E]; general liability.
operational_risks: Unpleasant work raises turnover; service consistency.
financial_risks: Low ticket; price pressure from janitorial bundling.
automation_potential: Scheduling, consumption tracking, billing.
scalability: Moderate; best as SKU on multi-service route.
expansion: First aid (WS13-004), scent (WS13-007), mats (WS13-006).
roic_note: Very low capital; ROIC high if routes dense [E].
critical_assumptions: Sufficient per-site revenue to justify visits
unanswered_questions: Illinois rules for sanitary waste disposal
score_rationale: Durable recurring need with low capital, but small tickets and bundling competition cap FCF.
preliminary_verdict: hold - add as SKU to WS13-004 route rather than standalone.

title: Entrance-mat rental and exchange using contract laundering (plant-free mat route)
product_service: Logo, scraper and anti-fatigue mats rented with weekly/bi-weekly exchange; laundering outsourced to a contract industrial laundry; optional outright mat sales.
target_customer: Retail, restaurants, offices, auto dealers, clinics, schools.
purchase_motivation: Slip-and-fall prevention, floor protection, branding.
spending_evidence: Industrial launderers (NAICS 812332): 329 firms, with $100M+ enterprises holding ~86% of receipts [C, WS13-S001]; Cintas sells entrance mats [A, WS13-S003] and agreed to acquire UniFirst in March 2026 [A, WS13-S004].
representative_operators: Cintas, UniFirst (merger agreement March 2026) [A, WS13-S004]
revenue_mechanism: Per-mat per-exchange fee; damage/replacement charges.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING; est. $4-$12 per mat per exchange [E].
direct_costs: Mat inventory (3-4 sets per placement), contract laundering, route labor, fuel.
contribution_profit_note: Highly dependent on laundering cost per lb, MISSING [E].
working_capital_note: Mat inventory float per customer; net-30.
customer_accessibility: Reachable; incumbents use multi-year auto-renew agreements [E].
supplier_accessibility: Unknown: contract industrial laundry capacity willing to serve a would-be competitor is unverified.
competitive_intensity: extreme - plant-scale incumbents with route density.
entry_strategy: Exploit post-merger service disruption; sell mats outright with periodic on-site cleaning instead of exchange.
licenses: None identified beyond business registration [E].
regulatory_barriers: Low (laundry wastewater rules fall on plant).
automation_potential: Limited: routing and billing.
scalability: Low without own plant (plant capex likely >$1M) [E].
expansion: Towels, mops (requires plant).
roic_note: Squeezed by laundering cost without plant; poor [E].
critical_assumptions: A contract laundry will serve a small route at viable price
unanswered_questions: Contract laundering cost per lb in Chicago
score_rationale: SUSB shows extreme concentration (86% of receipts at $100M+ firms): scale economics of plants dominate; plant-free entry has no cost wedge.
preliminary_verdict: reject - consolidation shows this is a plant-scale game; quiet money accrues to incumbents.

title: Commercial scent-marketing / ambient air-scenting subscription
product_service: Cold-air nebulizing diffusers (standalone or HVAC-integrated) installed at no/low upfront cost with monthly fragrance-oil refill subscription and servicing.
target_customer: Hotels, boutique retail, gyms, auto dealerships, senior living, salons, offices, casinos.
purchase_motivation: Brand experience, odor masking, perceived cleanliness.
spending_evidence: MISSING - incumbent sites (e.g., ScentAir) returned 403; no spend data retrieved [E].
representative_operators: ScentAir, Prolitec (names known to analyst; size not verified this session) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly subscription per diffuser incl. oil.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING; est. $50-$300 per diffuser per month [E].
direct_costs: Diffuser hardware, fragrance oils (minimum orders), service visits.
contribution_profit_note: Oil cost low relative to subscription if usage modest [E].
working_capital_note: Hardware capex per site recovered over 6-18 months [E].
customer_accessibility: Reachable but discretionary budget.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: diffusers and fragrance oils available from OEMs/fragrance houses [E].
entry_strategy: Local service + custom scents for regional brands.
licenses: None identified [E]; fragrance allergen/IAQ complaints possible.
automation_potential: Refill scheduling, remote diffuser control.
expansion: Odor control for senior living, restroom air care (WS13-005).
roic_note: Low capital; high gross margin; demand discretionary [E].
score_rationale: Consumable margin attractive but demand is discretionary and DIY diffusers erode pricing.
preliminary_verdict: hold - low evidence; only as add-on to hygiene route.

title: Commercial interiorscaping (plant leasing & maintenance) with seasonal holiday decor
product_service: Leased live/preserved plants and planters with weekly-biweekly watering/pruning and replacement guarantee; seasonal holiday decor design-install-removal for lobbies.
target_customer: Office building managers, hotels, hospitals, senior living, car dealerships, corporate campuses.
purchase_motivation: Lobby/brand presentation, tenant retention, biophilic design.
spending_evidence: Landscaping services (561730) has 114,842 firms, IL 4,949 [C, WS13-S001, WS13-S002]; interiorscape subset spend MISSING.
representative_operators: Ambius (Rentokil) - site inaccessible this session [E]
revenue_mechanism: Monthly maintenance/lease per plant; one-time holiday installs.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING; est. $150-$2,000 per site per month; holiday installs $2k-$25k [E].
direct_costs: Plants, planters, technician labor, replacements, decor inventory.
working_capital_note: Plant inventory up front; net-30.
customer_accessibility: Reachable; office demand weakened post-2020 [E].
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: Florida tropical nurseries ship to Chicago [E].
entry_strategy: Holiday decor first (urgent, seasonal) then convert to year-round maintenance.
licenses: Pesticide applicator license if applying pesticides indoors [A, WS13-S023].
automation_potential: Scheduling, photo-based plant health logging.
expansion: Exterior seasonal planters, holiday lighting.
roic_note: Moderate capital; good returns if contracts stable [E].
score_rationale: Recurring but discretionary and office-exposed.
preliminary_verdict: hold - modest ceiling and office exposure.

title: Restaurant back-of-house wear-parts route (refrigeration door gaskets, hood-filter exchange, strip curtains, knife/blade exchange)
product_service: Scheduled route that replaces torn refrigeration door gaskets (made to OEM spec), hinges/closers, walk-in strip curtains, swaps clean baffle hood filters on a cycle, and runs a sharpened-knife/slicer-blade exchange.
target_customer: Kitchen managers at independent and chain restaurants, grocery delis/meat departments, school and hospital kitchens.
purchase_motivation: Health-inspection findings (torn gaskets), energy loss, grease-fire risk from dirty filters, dull blades.
spending_evidence: Gasket Guy serves chains (e.g., Subway, Starbucks per page) with same/next-day service and monthly route rotations [D, WS13-S030]; Other Personal & Household Goods Repair (811490) and Commercial Machinery Repair (811310) are fragmented (811490: 10,622 firms, $100M+ share ~6% of receipts) [C, WS13-S001].
representative_operators: Gasket Guy - Midwest gasket replacement operator (D) [WS13-S030]
Local knife-sharpening route operators [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-door gasket installed price; filter exchange subscription per visit; knife exchange per knife per cycle.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING verified; est. $70-$200 per gasket installed, $30-$100 per filter-exchange visit [E].
direct_costs: Gasket material/fabrication, filters and cleaning, knives inventory, van, technician time.
contribution_profit_note: High per-visit margin; profit limited by visit volume [E].
working_capital_note: Low inventory; paid on service or net-15.
customer_accessibility: Very accessible; thousands of kitchens; low-ticket purchases don't need RFPs.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: gasket extrusion/welding equipment or made-to-order gasket suppliers available [E].
entry_strategy: Same-day service and bundling multiple wear parts in one visit.
licenses: None identified [E].
automation_potential: Routing, reorder reminders, photo-based gasket measurement.
scalability: Limited per metro; good as bundle on larger route.
expansion: Dishmachine/ice routes, hood cleaning referral (WS05).
roic_note: Capital under $15k; ROIC >300% possible but absolute profit small [E].
critical_assumptions: Bundling raises ticket enough to justify visits
score_rationale: Excellent access and ROIC, low ceiling standalone.
preliminary_verdict: hold - strong add-on module for a foodservice route (WS13-001/002), weak standalone.

title: Draft beer line cleaning & draft-system maintenance route for bars and restaurants

revenue_mechanism: Per-line per-cleaning fee or monthly contract.

customer_accessibility: High density of buyers in Chicago.

unanswered_questions: Illinois rules on who may clean lines
score_rationale: Cheap to start but low ceiling and possible tied-house complications.
preliminary_verdict: reject standalone - fold into bar/restaurant route bundle.

title: Standby-generator compliance services: diesel fuel testing/polishing and load-bank testing
product_service: Annual fuel sampling with lab analysis, fuel polishing/tank cleaning, biocide/stabilizer treatment, and portable load-bank testing for standby diesel generators; reports formatted for facility compliance files.

supplier_accessibility: Assumed: used containers available via depots/brokers [E].
